source.title: Think Global, Act Local: Relating DNN generalisation and node-level SNR

record.file_problem: Text appears complete; no obvious truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures different network properties and relates them to test accuracy, conceptually testing whether trained-network properties track generalization.
record.gate_note: The study reports correlations between node-level SNR measures and test accuracy. Its regularization discussion does not report an extractable dropout-versus-control test-error comparison. It does not test the specific claim versions about memorization, width, architecture, optimizer comparisons, batch size, dropout effects, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 compares MNIST test accuracy across unregularized SGD, L2 and dropout runs, directly bearing on V6. The supplied text does not preserve the plotted points needed to establish dropout's advantage. The SNR correlations themselves test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that node-level SNR optimality correlates with generalization and distinguishes weight configurations fitting the same dataset. They further propose mechanisms connecting regularization to SNR optimality. The empirical correlations do not establish causation, and the aggregate gain expression is explicitly described as empirically selected and not generally applicable.
record.recipe_differences: Measures node-level SNR optimality and SNR gain against test accuracy; it does not reproduce the claim versions' interventions or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported association varies by layer and dataset: combined layers 1–4 correlate clearly on CIFAR-10, while individual-layer relationships are described as weak; the final layer is more variable. On MNIST, the reported correlations differ by layer.

fits_no_version.finding: SNR gain correlates with test accuracy, with substantial dependence on dataset and layer aggregation. MNIST G2 has Spearman correlation 0.818; CIFAR-10 G(1..4) has 0.790, whereas CIFAR-10 G1 has 0.143 with p=0.065.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Empirically constructed node-level SNR measures track test accuracy in these networks, with limitations involving layer aggregation, outliers and softmax outputs.

record.problems: The study describes its SNR gain expression as empirically selected and not generally applicable; it relies on pragmatic assumptions and reports correlations rather than causal tests. The reported CIFAR-10 final-layer relationship is variable.
record.rows_left_out: No separate dropout, L2, or unregularized-SGD test-error comparison was extracted: the text does not give a specific comparative outcome, and Figure 1 does not provide recoverable per-condition values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: No random-label training or comparison of random-label and natural-label generalization.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No matched convolutional versus fully connected comparison; the architectures use different datasets.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance comparison.
No batch-size intervention or fixed-epoch comparison; the small-batch discussion is conjectural.

Very small training sets, excessive dropout, and removing dropout together with weight decay under augmentation are not tested. Figure 1 tests the basic dropout comparison, but its direction and size cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbation measure, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison against norm and margin measures.
No removal of memorized training examples or random-removal control.

missing.what: The authors report that selectively applying dropout to layers with poor SNR optimality improved a training scheme's performance. A row should preserve this qualitative report while marking the outcome metric, comparator details and effect size as unspecified; it cannot independently establish lower held-out error.

record.verdict_notes: The record's blanket classification of V6 as untested overlooks Figure 1's direct test-accuracy comparison across training schemes. Its unreadable group outcomes are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not added to missing. No V6 verdict is justified by the recoverable text: Section 4 does not identify which scheme performs better, and Section 7.3 does not identify its performance metric. All ten numerical rows remain outside the supplied versions; their states therefore describe inability to adjudicate those versions, not absence of the reported SNR correlations. Printed p-values of 0.000 are rounded values.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparisons.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning regimes.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Whether dropout changes held-out error, including the specified training-set and underfitting regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
